story.title: The Last Breakfast
story.logline: A man eats his morning toast, completely unaware that his entire life is an algorithm generating tomorrow's nostalgia.
story.theme: Manufactured reality and the commodification of human routine.
story.twist: He is not a living human remembering his past, but a real-time synthetic simulation whose final memory loop is bought by tourists.
story.ending: Would you pay to feel alive, if you knew the feeling was farmed?

scenes.narration: My toast always burns on the exact same corner, right at seven o'clock every single morning.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical framing. 30-year-old Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt in a cramped, sunlit kitchen, staring at burnt toast.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on the black edge of the bread, rapid zoom out.

scenes.narration: I reach for the chipped yellow mug, feeling the exact same warmth against my tired fingertips.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt in the cramped, sunlit kitchen, gripping a yellow mug.
scenes.camera: Medium shot, tracking his hand movement closely.

scenes.narration: Outside the kitchen window, the same blue sparrow freezes mid-air, waiting for my permission to move.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt looking out the window at a hovering bird.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder shot focusing on the motionless animal.

scenes.narration: A sharp knock echoes from the front door, though nobody has visited me in ten years.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt turning his head sharply toward a wooden door in the hallway.
scenes.camera: Low angle tracking shot moving down the narrow corridor.

scenes.narration: I open the heavy wood, and find a digital receipt floating in the empty hallway air.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt reaching out to touch a glowing holographic receipt.
scenes.camera: Push-in shot centering on the bright blue floating text.

scenes.narration: Bold letters across the glowing screen read: Simulation complete. Customer rating four point nine stars.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt illuminated by harsh blue light, staring at the floating text.
scenes.camera: Close-up on his wide, terrified eyes reflecting the code.

scenes.narration: My entire childhood, my first heartbreak, this very kitchen—all of it was just an expensive memory pack.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt watching his memories flash like dust motes in the air.
scenes.camera: Wide spinning shot around the dissolving room.

scenes.narration: A bored tourist in the real world is about to take off their headset and forget me completely.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt slowly turning translucent against a fading background.

scenes.narration: My fingers start to dissolve into golden pixels, yet I still taste the bitter coffee on my tongue.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo with messy brown hair and a faded blue t-shirt looking at his fading hands in the sunlit kitchen.
scenes.camera: Macro shot on fingertips turning into digital static.

scenes.narration: Would you pay to feel alive, if you knew the feeling was farmed?
scenes.visual_prompt: An empty kitchen, completely silent, with a burnt piece of toast sitting on a clean white plate.
scenes.camera: Static wide shot holding still in total emptiness.

caption.hook: His morning toast is someone else's memory.
caption.title: The Last Breakfast
caption.caption:
Every crunch, every sigh, every mundane second of his morning has already been bought and paid for. He thinks he's living a life, but he's just an algorithm generating tomorrow's nostalgia.

Would you pay to remember a life you never lived?
